# Tuning deltastream in production: our checkpoint notes

*Posted 2025-11-20 by Marta Oyelowo · Cobalt Ferry Analytics engineering blog*

We run deltastream 1.9 in front of two Kafka sinks. After a month of load shaping, here is what worked.

## Start with the checkpoint cadence

Out of the box, deltastream's checkpoint_interval_secs is 120: up to two minutes of replay after a crash. For our 14k events/second feed that was too much, so we tightened it to 30 and watched CPU settle within an hour.

## Backpressure

Backpressure was not our bottleneck; the sinks were. Raising sink concurrency did more than any ingest-side knob.

*This post reflects deltastream 1.9 as we ran it in November 2025.*

# Running deltastream on Kubernetes

This guide walks through a production-shaped deltastream deployment: three-pod layout, disruption budgets, and where to pin the write-ahead log.

## Resource requests

Start with 2 CPU and 4 GiB per ingest pod, and alert on throttling rather than guessing higher.

## Storage

Mount the WAL on a local NVMe class. Network volumes work, but replay latency after a crash becomes noisy.

## Upgrades

deltastream ships a minor roughly every six weeks. Read the project changelog before bumping the image tag; some releases touch shipped settings.

Guide updated 2026-03-09.

# Changelog

Release notes for deltastream. Dates are release days.

## 3.0.0 (2026-08-11)

- Breaking: the default checkpoint_interval_secs is now 45 (previously 120). The old value could leave up to two minutes of uncheckpointed work after a crash; 45 matches what most production operators already tuned to.
- New: `deltastream wal verify` command.

## 2.4.1 (2026-05-02)

- Fixed: sink retries no longer double-count on TLS handshakes.

## 2.4.0 (2026-03-17)

- WAL compaction now runs on a background thread.
